options.bet: Before and after: Leah's page in pencil; drag a line to see the app's red marks, with the app's summary card
options.benefit: Shows the value (the marking) on the real page; one simple interaction
options.cost: No phone in view; the scan step itself is not shown
options.risk: A parent may not see that the marks come from a phone app

options.bet: A real photo of a parent's phone over the workbook; the phone screen plays camera, marking, marked
options.benefit: Shows the act and the result in one picture; the most real
options.cost: Depends on one stock photo; the screen text is small
options.risk: A stock photo can feel staged; it needs a clean licence and a matching phone for production

options.bet: The marked page with the worked steps for one slip (question 19)
options.benefit: Shows the teaching, not only the marking
options.cost: The most text in the visual
options.risk: Reads like a worksheet answer key

options.bet: Text only: three large lines (more practice, less practice, a step ahead)
options.benefit: Quiet break before the closing cards; easy to read
options.cost: No picture of the next workbook
options.risk: Can feel thin next to the image-heavy steps above

options.bet: This workbook, then the next one: two covers with an arrow
options.benefit: Makes 'a new book each time' concrete
options.cost: Needs a real Workbook 04 cover design

options.bet: Built from: the scans, the session with Maya and the assessment feed into the next cover
options.benefit: Shows 'builds on all of it' literally
options.cost: The busiest visual on the page
options.risk: Repeats what the closing cards say
